They recall a foolish childhood argument about who could climb the tallest tree.
They remember an old teacher who was far stricter than either of them thought necessary.
They laugh about a terrible meal they once prepared together.
They remember a difficult season, and someone who helped them survive it.
They speak of a friend who is no longer there. For a while, neither knows what to say.
They realize they remember the same event differently. Neither insists on having the final word.
The visitor asks to meet the villager's family. They spend a pleasant afternoon together.
The two exchange a few stories, then go their separate ways. It is enough.
A child interrupts with an extremely personal question. Both adults laugh, grateful for the interruption.
The villager offers a small keepsake. The visitor accepts it with both hands.
"I thought you had forgotten me," the visitor admits. "Never," says the villager.
They part without resolving every difference between them. The next meeting will be easier.

intro.name: An old face
intro.text:
A former Heathen-born villager and an Isolan visitor meet near the edge of the village. They recognize each other from years ago.
For a moment, neither speaks.
The visitor notices {A}.
"You're different," says the visitor. "So are you," replies the villager.
